questions.question: What would you need to learn in your first 90 days to become effective as an IT System Business Analyst in a large healthcare organization, and how would you keep current on relevant industry trends?

A product owner changes a requirement halfway through a sprint after developers have begun work. As the business analyst, what steps would you take to analyze impact, update artifacts, and support a delivery decision?

This role requires at least five years of related experience. Walk us through which parts of your Data Analyst and Fraud Coordinator, team-lead, and other roles you consider directly relevant to IT system business analysis, and where you would need support initially.

What specifically motivates your transition from fraud and data analysis into an IT System Business Analyst role, and how would you use your payment, compliance, and stakeholder-reporting experience to add value in healthcare?
If asked to coach a junior business analyst who produces vague requirements, what feedback process, examples, and follow-up checks would you use to improve their work?

Describe how you would turn a request from a healthcare operations manager to reduce claim-processing rework into a set of validated business requirements, including stakeholders, assumptions, acceptance criteria, and open questions.

How would you translate a business requirement such as 'improve visibility into payment exceptions' into technical specifications for developers, including data fields, business rules, integrations, error handling, and testable acceptance criteria?
Show us how you would explain a complex data finding or system constraint to a non-technical healthcare stakeholder in clear English, then describe how you would confirm they understood it.
Walk us through the end-to-end business analysis lifecycle you would use from an initial business request through requirements approval, solution delivery, testing, and post-implementation review.

Describe any Agile environment you have worked in. If your prior work was not formally Agile, explain how you would participate in backlog refinement, sprint planning, daily stand-ups, reviews, and retrospectives.
